SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475


RESPONSE OF INTERVENOR JASON A. HOWTON TO THE CHAIRMAN'S MEMORANDUM PROPOSING REMAND
Intervenor Jason A. Howton, appearing pro se, respectfully files this response to the Chairman's Memorandum filed September 9, 2026 (Item No. 6514), which proposes to remand this proceeding to the State Office of Administrative Hearings, and would respectfully show as follows:
I. AUTHORITY TO FILE AND SCOPE
Intervenor Jason A. Howton files this response on two grounds.
First, the Commission's memorandum of September 9, 2026 states that "interested persons may file any comments regarding this matter in the Commission's Interchange under Docket Nos. 59182 and 59475."
Second, the Chairman's memorandum proposing remand was filed at 2:17 p.m. on September 9, 2026, the afternoon replies were due, and it proposes a disposition no party had briefed.
This response addresses only that proposed disposition. It raises no new ground on the merits, repeats no argument from Mr. Howton's Exceptions (Item No. 6456) or his Reply (Item No. 6517), and does not respond to any party's reply.
II. THE EXISTING RECORD PERMITS RESOLUTION OF ISSUES 11 AND 13; IF REMAND IS ORDERED, IT SHOULD BE ON THE CLOSED RECORD
The memorandum proposes remand because the Proposal for Decision "does not provide recommendations on preliminary order issues 11 and 13." It then states: "I do not know that it is necessary to reopen the record to address these issues, but I would defer to the judgment of the SOAH ALJs on this point."
That observation identifies an asserted omission in the Proposal for Decision's recommendations, not an identified deficiency in the evidentiary record. Rule 22.262(c)(1) expressly permits the Commission to remand for further consideration "with or without reopening the hearing" and to limit the issues considered.
A. The existing record permits resolution of Issues 11 and 13.
The existing record permits the Commission to resolve both issues without additional evidence.
On Issue 13, the Proposal for Decision states, and the memorandum acknowledges, that Applicants "did not submit evidence regarding the estimated congestion cost savings."
On Issue 11, the Administrative Law Judges found that Applicants presented the Project "as one that will import power from across the state of Texas into the Permian Basin and not that the proposed facilities [are] necessary to meet state or federal reliability standards."
Those findings establish what the existing record permits the decision-maker to find: Applicants did not establish that the facilities are necessary to meet any identified state or federal reliability standard, and they did not submit evidence quantifying estimated congestion cost savings.
Applicants bore the burden of proof under PURA § 37.056. Where the record lacks proof on an issue the Commission's Preliminary Order identified in advance, the absence of proof weighs against the party carrying that burden.
B. If the Commission remands for supplemental recommendations, the record should remain closed.
The memorandum acknowledges that addressing whether non-compliance with the relevant NERC standards "would result in violation of federal law" "may require additional briefing."
Briefing on the legal significance of evidence already admitted is materially different from reopening the evidentiary record. A remand that permits Applicants to introduce new evidence after the Proposal for Decision has identified deficiencies in their case would give them a post-decision opportunity to cure a failure of proof after the contested hearing and after the record closed.
Rule 22.262(c)(1) gives the Commission the narrower option: a limited remand on Issues 11 and 13 without reopening the hearing. Nothing in Texas Government Code § 2003.049 or Rule 22.262(c) requires the Commission to reopen the record simply because it seeks supplemental findings or recommendations.
Accordingly, if the Commission concludes that supplemental recommendations from the Administrative Law Judges are necessary, the remand order should expressly limit the remand to Issues 11 and 13 and direct that they proceed on the existing record.
Mr. Howton respectfully submits that the Commission should resolve Issues 11 and 13 on the existing record; if it remands, the remand should be limited to those issues and the record should remain closed.
III. PURA § 37.057 SETS SEPTEMBER 22, 2026, AND APPLICANTS HAVE TOLD THIS COMMISSION IT CANNOT BE EXTENDED
The Commission must decide this application by September 22, 2026.
That is eleven days after the open meeting at which remand is proposed, and the memorandum does not address the deadline.
Applicants have already told this Commission, in the very docket on which they principally rely, that the deadline admits of nothing. In Docket No. 59315 Oncor wrote that PURA § 37.057 contains "no 'good cause' exception, no tolling mechanism, and no provision authorizing the Commission or SOAH to suspend or continue the 180-day period."
Mr. Howton does not ask the Commission to adopt that reading because Oncor advanced it. He asks the Commission to note that the party that would benefit from remand is the party that has told this Commission remand cannot be accommodated within the statute.
Rule 22.52(a)(5) provides a specific day-for-day extension when its notice predicate is satisfied. 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(5) provides that "[f]ailure to provide notice in accordance with this section will be cause for day-for-day extension of deadlines for intervention and for commission action on the application."
If the Commission relies on that provision to create room for a remand, it must first identify the notice failure that triggers the extension, and that predicate is the Administrative Law Judges' conclusion, which is the opposite of the relief Applicants seek.
But Applicants themselves have argued that subsection (a)(5) does not extend to the public-meeting requirement in subsection (a)(4). Specifically, Applicants have told this tribunal that subsection (a)(5) "applies to failures to comply with the notice requirements for filing an application as set forth in 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(1)-(3)" and that "[n]othing in the text of the rule extends the day-for-day extension remedy to the public meeting context."
On Applicants' own construction, the public-meeting violation found by the Administrative Law Judges would not extend the statutory clock.
IV. THE PROPOSED REMAND DOES NOT REACH THE NOTICE GROUNDS, AND THE ORDER SHOULD SAY SO
The Administrative Law Judges recommended denial on two independent grounds. The memorandum addresses one of them.
Preliminary Order Issues 11 and 13 are both need issues; the proposed remand does not address the Proposal for Decision's separate notice findings.
The Proposal for Decision separately found that, after the June 2025 public meetings, Applicants added approximately 400 miles of new route links, bringing approximately 1,400 additional landowners within the class entitled to direct mail notice of the Application; held no further public meeting; and deprived those landowners of the public-meeting process.
The Proposal for Decision also separately found that Applicants did not use the county tax rolls current as of the filing date and that directly affected landowners were omitted from application notice.
Those findings and conclusions are outside the proposed remand and are fully briefed. The public-meeting findings and Conclusion of Law 15 separately support denial; the application-notice findings and Conclusion of Law 10 remain before the Commission.
The consequence matters. A remand ordered on need alone, without more, leaves ambiguous whether the notice findings return to the State Office of Administrative Hearings with the case. They should not. They were tried, found, excepted to, and replied to; the Commission has a complete record and complete briefing on them; and no party has asked that they be retried.
If the Commission remands, Mr. Howton respectfully requests that the order state expressly that the remand is limited to Preliminary Order Issues 11 and 13, that Findings of Fact 22 through 30 and 38 through 43 and Conclusions of Law 10, 11 and 15 are not remanded, and that the record is not reopened.
Mr. Howton further renews the request made in his Exceptions and Reply that, if the Commission changes any finding of fact or conclusion of law under Rule 22.262(a), it state in writing the specific reason and legal basis required by Rule 22.262(b) and Texas Government Code § 2003.049(h).
V. ORAL ARGUMENT
The memorandum states: "I still commit to granting oral argument in this case before any final decisions are made. So, I would defer all the requests for oral argument to be considered for a future open meeting."
Mr. Howton supports that commitment. Rule 22.262(d) permits oral argument before final disposition and authorizes the Commission to limit its scope and duration.
If the Commission concludes that legal argument or clarification of what the existing record establishes would assist it, the pending requests for oral argument provide a narrower alternative to reopening the evidentiary record.
Mr. Howton asks that, when oral argument is scheduled, the Commission allot time to an intervenor addressing the Bell County segment of the route, which no party, including Applicants, has defended on the record in either the exceptions round or the reply round.
VI. PRAYER
Mr. Howton respectfully requests that the Commission:
1. Decline to remand, resolve Preliminary Order Issues 11 and 13 on the existing record, and adopt the Administrative Law Judges' recommendation that the applications be denied;
2. In the alternative, if the Commission remands, enter an order that (a) limits the remand to Preliminary Order Issues 11 and 13, (b) directs the Administrative Law Judges to proceed on the existing record without reopening the hearing, (c) states that Findings of Fact 22 through 30 and 38 through 43 and Conclusions of Law 10, 11 and 15 are not remanded and remain before the Commission, and (d) states how the Commission will meet the deadline in PURA § 37.057;
3. Grant oral argument before any final decision, consistent with the Chairman's stated commitment; and
4. Grant such other and further relief to which he may be entitled.
SIGNATURE AND CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE
Respectfully submitted,
